intro_html: This Mediterranean bowl leans on roasted peppers and briny olives to make chicken taste like a vacation. It brings 61 grams of protein for about $4.18 a serving (at everyday cost), no fancy technique required. One batch makes 14 servings, so a few jars from the pantry aisle stretch a long way.
cost_closing_html: About $4.18 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each bowl delivers 61 grams of protein and 562 calories, a light but substantial plate.
upsell_html: A few smart pantry jars turn plain chicken into something worth looking forward to. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Jarred roasted red peppers and olives keep for ages, so stock a jar of each and pull them out whenever a meal needs a lift.
Onions and garlic are the cheap flavor backbone here, so always keep both in the house.
Bottled lime juice saves you from buying fresh citrus you'll let go bad, so keep a bottle in the fridge.
make_it: Add the chicken, sliced onion, chicken broth, olive oil, garlic, and lime juice to the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours until the chicken is tender all the way through.
Stir in the chopped roasted red peppers and olives during the last 30 minutes.
Shred the chicken into the pot so it soaks up the savory, briny juices.
Serve over white rice with plenty of the peppers and olives spooned on top.
